source_title: Is Your Code Generated by ChatGPT Really Correct? Rigorous Evaluation of Large Language Models for Code Generation (EvalPlus)
relevance: HumanEval+ expands HumanEval tests by 80x and reports catching previously undetected incorrect completions and changing some model rankings. Strong support that test strength can affect codegen evaluation, but it is Python/HumanEval evidence rather than a matched MultiPL-E cross-language replication.
status: official arXiv record reviewed; not added to sampled-cell denominator; no independent reproduction

source_title: LiveCodeBench: Holistic and Contamination Free Evaluation of Large Language Models for Code
relevance: Collects newly published contest problems and evaluates generation plus other code-related tasks; supports freshness/task-scope considerations, but is not a multilingual translation experiment.
status: official arXiv record reviewed; not added to sampled-cell denominator; no independent reproduction

source_title: AST-Probe: Recovering abstract syntax trees from hidden representations of pre-trained language models
relevance: Reports AST recovery from pretrained-model representations, so syntax probing itself is established; motivates shifting the lead to predictive validity against downstream correctness rather than whether syntax is encoded.
status: official arXiv record reviewed; not added to sampled-cell denominator; no independent reproduction

source_title: Unveiling Code Pre-Trained Models: Investigating Syntax and Semantics Capacities
relevance: Studies syntax and semantic structures across seven code models and reports differences between syntactic strengths and more variable semantic representations; reinforces that structural probe outcomes and task competence should be separated.
status: official arXiv record reviewed; not added to sampled-cell denominator; no independent reproduction

source_title: Cross Project Software Vulnerability Detection via Domain Adaptation and Max-Margin Principle
relevance: Directly studies cross-project SVD with domain adaptation and reports improvements over baselines; means cross-project transfer itself is not an unexplored question.
status: official arXiv record reviewed; not added to sampled-cell denominator; no independent reproduction

source_title: Software Vulnerability Prediction Knowledge Transferring Between Programming Languages
relevance: Studies transfer from C training data to Java evaluation on SARD/VDISC and reports average recall; narrows any follow-up to fair, controlled, held-out transfer comparisons rather than claiming cross-language transfer has not been attempted.
status: official arXiv record reviewed; not added to sampled-cell denominator; no independent reproduction
